title: Counting the Days of a Billing Period by the Movement the Bin Saw
content:
The days billed in a storage period are counted by the movement the bin saw, because the lot is re-weighed and the bin re-gauged when it is topped up. This rule governs billing periods on Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## Standing rule

Where the last load into store arrived inside the period and no bushels left store inside it, the days are counted from the day that load arrived through the last day of the period, both days counted. Where bushels left store inside the period and no load arrived inside it, the days are counted from the first day of the period through the day the last bushels left, both days counted. And otherwise every day of the period is billed.

## The four combinations set out

| A load arrived inside the period | Bushels left store inside the period | Days counted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | no | from the day the last load arrived through the last day of the period, both days counted |
| no | yes | from the first day of the period through the day the last bushels left, both days counted |
| yes | yes | every day of the period |
| no | no | every day of the period |

The two middle cases of the table are the same result reached two ways: where the bin saw both kinds of movement, and where it saw neither, the whole period is counted.

## Worked counts, on a hypothetical period

Take a period running from 1 June through 30 June, thirty days long.

**A load arrives on 12 June and nothing leaves.** The days run from 12 June through 30 June inclusive, which is 19 days.

**Bushels leave on 12 June and nothing arrives.** The days run from 1 June through 12 June inclusive, which is 12 days.

**A load arrives on 8 June and bushels leave on 21 June.** Both kinds of movement fell inside the period, so every day of the period is billed, which is 30 days.

**Nothing moves at all.** Every day of the period is billed, which is 30 days.

## Notes

**Are the boundary days counted?** They are. Where the count starts from the day a load arrived, that day is counted; where it ends on the day the last bushels left, that day is counted too.

**What makes the first case different from the third?** In the first, only one kind of movement fell inside the period, so the count is shortened to the part of the period the bin stood as it now stands. In the third, both kinds fell inside it, and the whole period is counted.
